_doc: THE LANGUAGE OF THE PIECE (decibel PLAN 2.3; RUNNING_LOG §307; DEC-90: 'the piece uses a variation of anthony braxton's language musics, we will use the badges from p1&2, that format and then come up with a symbal for each and a color'). `badge`: the format, read from piece #1's flocking badge (string_quartet_no1-composer/docs/notation_instructions/images/flocking_badge.svg). `types`: HIS six, in his order — each the piece's own sound type, the Braxton Language Type it varies (his handout's number, name and sign, described in words; the handout itself is at the Library of Congress), and where it is in the piece. A type's `symbol` and `colour` are EMPTY until he chooses. `candidates.<type>`: signs put to him — each an icon drawn in a 36 × 36 box (`svg`, in currentColor), where it comes from, what speaks for it. tools/language/build_page.js draws them as badges on score/public/language/index.html. A candidate's `svg` may hold `<glyph name='articulation.trill' x='..' y='..' h='..'/>`: the builder replaces it with THAT glyph's outline from notation/lib/glyphs.json — the notation's own font (LilyPond's Emmentaler) — its top-left at x, y, scaled to the height h. A type with a `symbol` (a candidate's id) and a `colour` (a name of sol.json or clr.json) is CHOSEN: the page shows its badge and no longer its candidates.

badge.from: piece #1 (the flocking badge): a 36 px rounded square of dark slate, the sign in it in light blue. Piece #2's badge (the three orbits) is black discs and lines on white, no square.

types.name: short attacks

types.inThePiece: the opening's impulses · the three body problem

types.name: multiphonics

braxton.name: MULTIPHONICS

types.name: audible beats
types.inThePiece: the beating section — a held note against a sine
types.nameFrom: his choice 2026-10-09 (DEC-91) — Alvin Lucier's own phrase: "their oscillations periodically coincide to produce audible beats of sound" (Crossings)

types.name: scattered strikes
types.inThePiece: section 5 — the ensemble's strikes, the electronics answering

braxtonTwelve: 2 Accented long sound — a narrow wedge that runs on as a line
3 Trills — a line of tall waves
4 Staccato line formings — a dashed line
5 Intervallic formings — a line that jumps up and down in square steps
7 Short attacks — three small open triangles
8 Angular attacks — a chain of sharp Z shapes
9 Legato formings — a long smooth wave
10 Diatonic formings — a smooth wave with small strokes across it
11 Gradient formings — a smooth wave with arrowheads along it
12 Sub-identity formings — a small square, then a line

shortAttacks.name: Braxton's own
shortAttacks.from: Language Type 7, his handout: three small open triangles, two pointing left and one up
shortAttacks.for: It IS the sign of the language the piece varies. A player who knows Braxton reads it at once.
shortAttacks.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.6' stroke-linejoin='round'><polygon points='12,14 12,23 5,18.5'/><polygon points='21.5,13.5 21.5,22 15,17.8'/><polygon points='27.5,13.5 31.5,22.5 23.5,22.5'/></g>

shortAttacks.name: marcato
shortAttacks.from: the standard sign for a marked, forceful attack — an open wedge over the note
shortAttacks.for: His candidate. Every player knows it. One clean shape, readable at 36 px.
shortAttacks.svg: <polyline points='9.5,26 18,9.5 26.5,26' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3.2' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='miter'/>

shortAttacks.name: marcato, scattered
shortAttacks.from: the marcato wedge, three times, at uneven heights
shortAttacks.for: Says SEVERAL attacks, irregular — closer to what the type is than one accent; keeps the known sign.
shortAttacks.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2.3' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='miter'><polyline points='4,22 8.5,12.5 13,22'/><polyline points='13.5,28 18,18.5 22.5,28'/><polyline points='23,17.5 27.5,8 32,17.5'/></g>

shortAttacks.name: staccatissimo, scattered
shortAttacks.from: the standard sign for the shortest note — a small solid wedge — three times
shortAttacks.for: It means SHORT, where the marcato means MARKED. A solid triangle: Braxton's shape, filled.

shortAttacks.name: staccato dots, scattered
shortAttacks.for: The plainest. Risk: three dots read as an ellipsis, or as nothing, at this size.
shortAttacks.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><circle cx='8' cy='20' r='2.7'/><circle cx='18' cy='13' r='2.7'/><circle cx='28' cy='23' r='2.7'/></g>

shortAttacks.name: marcato, scattered — the notation font's own
shortAttacks.from: the marcato of the score's font (LilyPond's Emmentaler), three times, where the chosen sign has its three
shortAttacks.for: The same sign he chose, drawn by the font the staff uses: thicker on one stroke, as engraved.
shortAttacks.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='articulation.marcato' x='4.2' y='12.6' h='9.6'/><glyph name='articulation.marcato' x='13.7' y='18.6' h='9.6'/><glyph name='articulation.marcato' x='23.2' y='8.1' h='9.6'/></g>

trills.name: Braxton's own
trills.from: Language Type 3, his handout: a line of tall, deep waves
trills.for: The sign of the language the piece varies. It also LOOKS like the sound: a line shaking.
trills.svg: <path fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-linecap='round' d='M4,18 c1.6,-12 4,-12 5.6,0 s4,12 5.6,0 s4,-12 5.6,0 s4,12 5.6,0 s4,-12 5.6,0'/>

trills.name: tr
trills.from: the trill sign of the score's own font (LilyPond's Emmentaler, scripts.trill) — the tr every player has read since the early 1700s
trills.for: His ask. Unmistakable, and the SAME glyph the staff shows over a trilled note.

trills.name: tr with its wavy line
trills.from: the standard full form: tr, then the wavy line that runs for as long as the trill lasts
trills.for: Says a trill that LASTS — the piece's trills are long, each into a petal hit.
trills.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='articulation.trill' x='2.6' y='10.6' h='14.5'/></g><path fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-linecap='round' d='M19.6,19.6 q1.1,-3.6 2.25,0 t2.25,0 2.25,0 2.25,0 2.25,0 2.25,0'/>

trills.name: tr with Braxton's wave
trills.from: the font's tr, then Braxton's tall deep wave in place of the standard wavy line
trills.for: Both languages in one badge: the sign players know, the wave of the language the piece varies.
trills.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='articulation.trill' x='2.2' y='10.6' h='14.5'/></g><path fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.8' stroke-linecap='round' d='M19.2,18 c1.2,-9.5 3.4,-9.5 4.6,0 s3.4,9.5 4.6,0 s3.4,-9.5 4.6,0'/>

trills.name: the wavy line alone
trills.from: the Baroque trill sign, the chevron — a short wavy line over the note, with no tr
trills.for: One stroke, the oldest form. Risk: at this size it can read as vibrato, or as plain decoration.
trills.svg: <path fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2.5' stroke-linecap='round' d='M4.8,18 q1.65,-5.4 3.3,0 t3.3,0 3.3,0 3.3,0 3.3,0 3.3,0 3.3,0 3.3,0'/>

trills.name: the cross
trills.from: the + of French Baroque scores, drawn with the font's own plus
trills.for: Shown for the record. It stood for almost any ornament then, and today it means a stopped note or a left-hand pizzicato — the wrong reading for these players.

accentedLongTones.name: Braxton's own
accentedLongTones.from: Language Type 2, his handout: a narrow closed wedge that runs on as a line — the accent, then the long sound
accentedLongTones.for: The sign of the language the piece varies. It is also a PICTURE of the sound: struck wide, thinning at once, then held.
accentedLongTones.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.6' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-linecap='round'><path d='M4,13.2 L4,22.8 L17.5,18 Z'/><line x1='17.5' y1='18' x2='32' y2='18'/></g>

accentedLongTones.name: the wedge, solid
accentedLongTones.from: Braxton's shape filled in: a solid wedge thinning into the line
accentedLongTones.for: The same picture, bolder — it holds at 36 px where the outline thins out. It is the shape of an attack that decays into a held tone.
accentedLongTones.svg: <path fill='currentColor' d='M4,12 L4,24 L18.5,19 L32,19 L32,17 L18.5,17 Z'/>

accentedLongTones.name: accent, then a line
accentedLongTones.from: the accent of the score's own font, and a line after it — as this score already draws a long tone: a sign, then its duration line
accentedLongTones.for: The known sign for the attack, the house's own sign for length. Reads left to right as it sounds.
accentedLongTones.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='articulation.accent' x='3.2' y='13.9' h='8.2'/><rect x='19.6' y='16.9' width='13.2' height='2.2' rx='1.1'/></g>

accentedLongTones.name: accent over tenuto
accentedLongTones.from: the standard pair, both from the score's font: the accent above, the tenuto line under it — marked AND held for its full length
accentedLongTones.for: Every player reads it at once. It is an articulation, though: it says how to play a note, less what kind of sound the type is.
accentedLongTones.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='articulation.accent' x='10.4' y='9.2' h='8.5'/><glyph name='articulation.tenuto' x='8.6' y='23.4' h='2.5'/></g>

accentedLongTones.name: fp
accentedLongTones.from: the forte-piano of the score's own font: suddenly loud, at once soft, and held
accentedLongTones.for: Says the DYNAMIC shape exactly. Risk: it reads as a dynamic to obey on one note, not as the name of a kind of sound.

multiphonics.name: Braxton's own
multiphonics.from: Language Type 6, his handout: three small five-sided shapes, like little houses — one upright, two upside down
multiphonics.for: The sign of the language the piece varies. Abstract: it does not look like the sound, so it must be learned once.

multiphonics.name: a chord of open noteheads
multiphonics.from: the commonest way a multiphonic is written: its sounding pitches as a chord — here three open heads of the score's own font, unevenly spaced
multiphonics.for: What a player already sees over a multiphonic. Says: several pitches at once, from one instrument.
multiphonics.svg: <g fill='currentColor'><glyph name='notehead.open' x='13.9' y='5.2' h='6.6'/><glyph name='notehead.open' x='13.9' y='12.2' h='6.6'/><glyph name='notehead.open' x='13.9' y='23.6' h='6.6'/></g>

multiphonics.name: three lines, stacked
multiphonics.from: Braxton's long-sound line, three times, one above another — several long sounds at once
multiphonics.for: A picture of the piece's multiphonics, which are HELD: recorded for 6 to 9 seconds and stretched into drones. Sits beside the accented long tone's wedge-and-line.
multiphonics.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linecap='round'><line x1='5' y1='11' x2='31' y2='11'/><line x1='5' y1='18' x2='24' y2='18'/><line x1='5' y1='25' x2='29' y2='25'/></g>

multiphonics.name: M in a circle
multiphonics.from: a marking some composers use: an encircled M over the note (guitar scores); cellists label a multiphonic M with its partials
multiphonics.for: Short and unmistakable once known. A letter, though, where every other badge so far is a sign.
multiphonics.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor'><circle cx='18' cy='18' r='12.6' stroke-width='1.6'/><polyline points='11.6,24.6 11.6,11.6 18,20.6 24.4,11.6 24.4,24.6' stroke-width='2.1' stroke-linejoin='miter' stroke-linecap='round'/></g>

multiphonics.name: a stack of diamonds
multiphonics.from: the diamond notehead — the sign of a harmonic — three times, stacked
multiphonics.for: Fits the strings, whose multiphonics are found at harmonic nodes. Risk: a diamond means different things on different instruments, and here it would read as harmonics.
multiphonics.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.7' stroke-linejoin='round'><polygon points='13.2,7.4 18,3.7 22.8,7.4 18,11.1'/><polygon points='13.2,15.6 18,11.9 22.8,15.6 18,19.3'/><polygon points='13.2,27.2 18,23.5 22.8,27.2 18,30.9'/></g>
